title: SQL injection in bad libuser.login
snippet: c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{}' and password = '{}'".format(username, password))

refs.note: string-format SQL with username and password

evidence: user = c.execute(SELECT FROM users WHERE username format username password).fetchone() | alt: c.execute(INSERT INTO users percent formatting username password) | validator: bad/libuser.py:12 SELECT with .format(username,password) reaches sqlite3 execute; reachable unauthenticated via bad/mod_user.py:16-20 request.form username/password -> libuser.login | consensus: 1/1 confirmed
rationale: WHO remote unauthenticated user controls username and password form fields. HOW bad mod_user do_login passes them to libuser.login which interpolates both into SELECT via format with no parameterization. WHAT breaks SQL syntax boundary allowing auth bypass and extraction.
hunter_evidence: user = c.execute(SELECT FROM users WHERE username format username password).fetchone() | alt: c.execute(INSERT INTO users percent formatting username password)
hunter_snippet: user = c.execute(SELECT FROM users WHERE username format username password).fetchone()
patch_summary: Use parameterized query: c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=? and password=?", (username,password)).

title: Broken authentication: unsigned base64 session cookie allows forgery

taint.sink: server trusts client-controlled session dict for authorization

refs.note: create: base64 JSON with no signature
sink/trust: json.loads(b64decode(cookie)) with bare except pass

evidence: bad/libsession.py:18-20 base64+json decode with no HMAC; bad/vulpy.py:42 before_request trusts g.session username for all authz | validator: bad/libsession.py:6 creates base64(JSON) with no MAC; bad/libsession.py:12-24 load() trusts client cookie via b64decode+json.loads with bare except; bad/vulpy.py:42 assigns g.session for all authz (bad/mod_posts.py:28, bad/mod_mfa.py:60) | consensus: 1/1 confirmed
rationale: Session cookie is plain base64(JSON) with no integrity. Anyone can craft base64({"username":"admin"}) and become admin. All route auth checks (posts, chpasswd, mfa) trust g.session derived from this cookie, so forgery spans session helper to every guarded handler.
hunter_evidence: bad/libsession.py:18-20 base64+json decode with no HMAC; bad/vulpy.py:42 before_request trusts g.session username for all authz
patch_summary: Replace client cookie with random server-side session or HMAC/Fernet-signed token and validate integrity/expiry on load.

title: API mass-assignment allows forging posts as arbitrary user

taint.source: POST /api/post JSON body username plus X-APIKEY header

evidence: bad/mod_api.py:57 authenticates as self, bad/mod_api.py:62 overwrites username from request JSON, bad/mod_api.py:69 writes post as forged username; post_schema at bad/mod_api.py:21 allows extra properties | validator: bad/mod_api.py:57 auth username in data then bad/mod_api.py:62 data.update(request.get_json()) overwrites it; bad/mod_api.py:21-28 post_schema lacks additionalProperties:False so forged username passes validate and bad/mod_api.py:69 libposts.post writes as victim | consensus: 1/1 confirmed
rationale: Authenticated attacker with any valid X-APIKEY can forge posts as arbitrary user. do_post_create stores authenticate() result in data['username'] then unconditionally overwrites it with attacker JSON via data.update(request.get_json()) before validation; post_schema lacks additionalProperties:false so extra username passes, and libposts.post writes with forged username. hunter_evidence: bad/mod_api.py:57 authenticates as self, bad/mod_api.py:62 overwrites username from request JSON, bad/mod_api.py:69 writes post as forged username; post_schema at bad/mod_api.py:21 allows extra properties

title: Glob-injection arbitrary file deletion in API key rotation

taint.sink: Path.glob + unlink on attacker-controlled pattern in /tmp

refs.note: key file path also built from same username

evidence: bad/mod_api.py:39 flows JSON username into bad/libapi.py:16 glob pattern; username='*' matches all vulpy.apikey files and f.unlink deletes them | validator: bad/libapi.py:16 glob('vulpy.apikey.'+username+'.*') with bad/libapi.py:18 f.unlink() reachable from bad/mod_api.py:39 with no username validation; bad/mod_user.py:38 allows creating '*' user | consensus: 1/1 confirmed
rationale: Username is concatenated into a Path.glob pattern then every match is unlinked. Wildcards (*,?,[]) in attacker username expand to other users' key files, allowing an authenticated (or empty-password-bypassed) user to delete all API keys (DoS) and interfere with auth state. Distinct sink from authenticate() glob bypass: this is file deletion in keygen cleanup.

title: API authentication bypass via glob injection in /tmp key lookup

refs.note: sink: Path glob with concatenated key

evidence: bad/mod_api.py:54-57 X-APIKEY header flows into bad/libapi.py:30 glob pattern; '*' matches any key file and returns victim username | validator: bad/libapi.py:28 X-APIKEY header flows unsanitized into bad/libapi.py:30 Path.glob('vulpy.apikey.*.'+key) returning bad/libapi.py:31 split('.')[2]; reachable unauthenticated via bad/mod_api.py:54 do_post_create | consensus: 1/1 confirmed

hunter_evidence: bad/mod_api.py:54-57 X-APIKEY header flows into bad/libapi.py:30 glob pattern; '*' matches any key file and returns victim username
patch_summary: Store keys server-side indexed by exact key hash and compare with hmac.compare_digest; reject glob metacharacters and never use glob as auth decision.
